title: Show why a matched state and one known nonzero load do not identify target power
statement: The passive reciprocal two-ports [[0,1/4],[1/4,0]] and [[0,1/5],[1/5,18/25]] have identical returns at z=0 and1/2 for every input but matched target powers1/16 and1/25. The third load -1/2 distinguishes them.

requires: Matched state and one calibrated nonzero load only
Unknown feedback pole and target coupling
provides: Exact all-command indistinguishability witness under coherent accessible measurements
assumptions: This is not a minimality theorem for every different instrument or prior
costs: Charge all raw powers,reference/signal photons,combiner loss,calibration,mask writes,load switching,settling and reset;no free parameter,clock or arbitrarily strong local oscillator.
contract.units: Dimensionless power per incident feed-power unit;field amplitude is its square root. r,z,s are complex reflection amplitudes;R is reference amplitude. Physical photon/time calibration remains an acquired input.
contract.obstruction: Do not replace the general unknown-background three-load construction by arbitrary two-state switching.
